s1.syndrome_frame: A congenital, exophytic, smooth, and soft lesion on the dorsal tongue
salient_findings: 1.5-cm diameter lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion has been present since birth
MRI showed a partly fatty, submucosal mass with mild contrast enhancement
key_facts: 20-year-old man with no significant medical history
1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion has been present since birth
Lesion has not changed in size or character
Vital signs were within normal limits
MRI showed a 1.5-cm protuberant mass arising from the dorsal aspect of the tongue
Lesion appeared partly fatty, likely submucosal
Mild contrast enhancement on MRI
Intact overlying mucosa
No involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles
Sublingual space and major salivary glands appeared normal

differentials: Solitary fibrous tumor of the tongue

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Partly fatty lesion on MRI, consistent with lipoma

shortlist.label: Leiomyomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Smooth muscle component possible, given lesion's characteristics

shortlist.label: Choristoma
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital lesion with potential for mixed tissue types

shortlist.label: Fibrous epithelial polyp
shortlist.why_kept: Exophytic and smooth lesion, could be a benign polyp

shortlist.label: Hamartoma of the tongue
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital lesion with potential for disordered growth of tongue tissues

raw.rationale: The lesion's appearance as partly fatty on MRI and its soft, exophytic nature are consistent with a lipoma, a benign tumor composed of fat tissue.

rejected.label: Leiomyomatous hamartoma
rejected.why: While possible, the lack of specific muscular or leiomyomatous characteristics in the description makes this less likely

rejected.label: Choristoma
rejected.why: Choristomas are rare and typically contain tissue not native to the area, which is not indicated here

rejected.label: Fibrous epithelial polyp
rejected.why: These are usually more pedunculated and less likely to be partly fatty

rejected.label: Hamartoma of the tongue
rejected.why: Hamartomas are disorganized tissue growths, but the specific characteristics of this lesion, such as being partly fatty, do not strongly suggest a hamartoma
